mainTopic: Two sources for why both father and ארוס cancel a נערה המאורסה's vows, and the בעיא of whether the ארוס 'cuts' or 'weakens' the vow
overview: The גמרא brings a second source, from the school of רבי ישמעאל, for the rule that a נערה המאורסה's vows are cancelled by her father and her ארוס together. It then asks how each side uses the other side's פסוק. רבי ישמעאל's school uses 'אם היו תהיה לאיש' for רבא's other teaching. רבא uses 'בין איש לאשתו' to teach that a husband cancels only vows that affect the two of them. Next the גמרא asks a new question: when the ארוס cancels, does he cut away his share of the vow, or weaken the whole vow? The practical difference is a case of two olives, where the answer decides whether she gets מלקות. To answer, the גמרא begins a ברייתא about when the father's power becomes complete after the ארוס dies, and the ברייתא continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The school of רבי ישמעאל gives a different source
steps.stepSummary: דבי רבי ישמעאל learn from 'between a man and his wife, between a father and his daughter' that the father and the ארוס together cancel a נערה המאורסה's vows.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: 'Between a man and his wife, between a father and his daughter.' From here we learn that a betrothed young girl's father and husband together cancel her vows.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source for the rule in the משנה that a נערה המאורסה needs both her father and her ארוס to cancel her vows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the rule came from רבא's reading of 'אם היו תהיה לאיש'. Here דבי רבי ישמעאל point to a different פסוק, which names the husband and the father in the same breath. That pairing tells us both are involved in cancelling her vows.

keyTerms.meaning: The school (study house) of רבי ישמעאל
Taught (a ברייתא teaching)
A young girl who is betrothed but not yet married
Cancel (vows), from הֲפָרָה

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
"Between a man and his wife,
between a father and his daughter"
from here we learn about a betrothed young girl
that her father and her husband cancel her vows.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second source, alongside רבא's, for the same rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Father and ארוס jointly cancel a נערה המאורסה's vows, learned from 'בין איש לאשתו בין אב לבתו'.

steps.title: What does רבי ישמעאל's school do with 'if she be to a husband'?
steps.stepSummary: If דבי רבי ישמעאל get the rule from another פסוק, what do they learn from 'אם היו תהיה לאיש'?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to the תנא of the school of רבי ישמעאל, what does he do with 'and if she be to a husband'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the school of רבי ישמעאל learns from the פסוק that רבא used as his source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The assumption is that no words of the תורה are extra. Since דבי רבי ישמעאל take the rule from a different פסוק, 'אם היו תהיה לאיש' must teach them something else.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And if she be to a husband', the פסוק רבא used
What does he do with it? (what does he learn from it)

phrases.english: And according to the Tanna of the school of Rabbi Yishmael,
"and if she be to a husband"
what does he do with it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְתָנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אִם הָיוֹ תִהְיֶה לְאִישׁ מַאי עָבֵיד לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the new source's author uses the older source's פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What דבי רבי ישמעאל derive from 'אם היו תהיה לאיש'.

steps.title: They use it for רבא's other teaching
steps.stepSummary: דבי רבי ישמעאל use 'אם היו תהיה לאיש' for רבא's other teaching.
steps.simpleTranslation: He uses it for the other teaching of רבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the school of רבי ישמעאל uses that פסוק for a different teaching of רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא learned two things from this פסוק. דבי רבי ישמעאל already have a source for the joint cancellation, so they only use the פסוק for רבא's second teaching. That way no word of the פסוק goes unused.

keyTerms.meaning: Establishes / applies (a פסוק to a teaching)
The other one

phrases.english: He applies it to the other teaching of Rava.
phrases.notes: רבא's other teaching: if the ארוס dies without upholding her vow, the father can cancel it alone.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'אם היו תהיה לאיש' teaches רבא's other rule.

steps.title: What does רבא do with the פסוק of רבי ישמעאל's school?
steps.stepSummary: The question is turned around: what does רבא learn from 'בין איש לאשתו'?
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא, what does he do with this פסוק that the school of רבי ישמעאל taught?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא flips the question and asks what רבא learns from the פסוק that the school of רבי ישמעאל used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא gets the joint cancellation from 'אם היו תהיה לאיש'. So 'בין איש לאשתו בין אב לבתו' must teach him something else.

keyTerms.meaning: This that (they) taught

phrases.aramaic: וְרָבָא, הַאי דְּתָנֵי דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
phrases.english: And Rava, this that the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught,
what does he do with it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרָבָא הַאי דְּתָנֵי דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל מַאי עָבֵיד לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirror question to step 2, now aimed at רבא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What רבא derives from 'בין איש לאשתו'.

steps.title: A husband only cancels vows that affect the two of them
steps.stepSummary: רבא uses 'בין איש לאשתו' to teach that the husband cancels only vows between him and her.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs it to teach that the husband cancels the vows that are between him and her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבא uses this פסוק to limit which vows a husband may cancel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבא, 'בין איש לאשתו' is a limit, not a source. A husband can cancel only vows that touch their relationship, called נדרים שבינו לבינה, and not every vow she makes. Both sides now have a use for both פסוקים.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it (for another teaching)
Vows that affect the relationship between husband and wife

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides agree that the father and the ארוס cancel together. They only disagree about which פסוק is the source, and each side finds another use for the other פסוק.

phrases.english: He needs it to say
that the husband cancels vows
that are between him and her.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לוֹמַר שֶׁהַבַּעַל מֵיפֵר נְדָרִים שֶׁבֵּינוֹ לְבֵינָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4 and closes this section.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'בין איש לאשתו' limits the husband to נדרים שבינו לבינה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a basic limit on a husband's power of הפרה. He may cancel only vows that touch their relationship.

steps.title: Does the ארוס cut the vow or weaken it?
steps.stepSummary: A new question: when the ארוס cancels, does he cut away his share of the vow, or weaken the whole vow?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: does a husband cut, or does he weaken?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about how the ארוס's cancellation actually works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two ways to picture it. Maybe he cuts off his half, so half the vow is gone and half stays in full force. Or maybe he weakens the whole vow, so all of it still exists but at reduced strength until the father also cancels.

keyTerms.meaning: They asked (an open question in the בית מדרש)
He cuts (cuts off his part completely)
He weakens (the whole vow)

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides agree she may not eat yet, because the father has not cancelled. The question is only about how strong the leftover prohibition is.

phrases.english: They asked:
Does the husband cut,
or does he weaken?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ בַּעַל מִיגָּז גָּיֵיז אוֹ מִקְלָישׁ קָלֵישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about how the ארוס's הפרה works.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the ארוס's הפרה removes his share entirely or weakens the whole vow.

steps.title: The case where the question matters: two olives
steps.stepSummary: The question matters when she vowed off two olives, the ארוס cancelled, and she ate both.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where does our question matter? For example, she vowed off two olives, her ארוס heard and cancelled for her, and she ate them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up a specific case where the two views give different results. This prepares the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case has a vow on exactly two olives and a cancellation by the ארוס only, not yet by the father. She then eats both olives. This case is built to test whether a full olive's worth of prohibition is still left.

keyTerms.meaning: Where does our question come up?
Olives
Betrothed husband

phrases.english: Where is our question relevant?
For example, where she vowed off two olives,
and the betrothed heard and cancelled it for her,
and she ate them.
phrases.notes: She ate them before the father cancelled his part.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the practical case for the question in step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The case where the difference between cutting and weakening shows up.

steps.title: מלקות or only an איסור: what is the ruling?
steps.stepSummary: If he cuts, she gets מלקות. If he weakens, she has only broken a lesser איסור. The גמרא asks which is right.
steps.simpleTranslation: If we say he cuts, she gets lashes. If we say he weakens, it is just a plain prohibition. What is the ruling?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the result each view gives in the olive case and then asks which view is correct.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he cuts off his half, one whole olive stays fully forbidden, so eating it brings מלקות. If he weakens the vow, neither olive is fully forbidden, so she has broken only an איסור בעלמא without מלקות. The גמרא asks 'מאי?' to request a ruling, and the next step brings a ברייתא to try to answer it.

keyTerms.meaning: She is lashed (gets מלקות)
Merely a prohibition, with no מלקות

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how a question about how הפרה works on the inside leads to a real halachic difference: whether she gets מלקות.

phrases.english: If we say he cuts, she is lashed.
phrases.notes: Half the vow is fully gone, so one whole olive is still fully forbidden.

phrases.english: If we say he weakens,
it is merely a prohibition.
What is it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the outcome of each view in the case from step 7 and asks for a ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether she receives מלקות, which depends on cutting versus weakening.

steps.title: A ברייתא: when the husband dies, the father's power takes over
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to answer the question. It opens by explaining when the rule 'if the husband dies, power goes to the father' applies: when the husband never heard the vow, or heard and stayed silent, or heard, cancelled, and died that same day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: When did they say that if the husband dies, the power to cancel goes back fully to the father? When the husband did not hear the vow before he died, or he heard and was silent, or he heard, cancelled, and died on that same day. This is what we learned in the משנה: if the husband dies, the power goes back to the father.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins quoting a ברייתא that it hopes will answer the question from the last step. This is only the opening part; the actual proof comes as the ברייתא continues.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the father and the ארוס cancel a נערה המאורסה's vows together. This ברייתא lists three cases where, after the ארוס dies, the father can cancel on his own. The third case, where the ארוס already cancelled and then died, matters for our question about what his cancellation actually did to the vow.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: the גמרא is bringing a source to answer a question
The power to cancel goes fully over to the father
He heard the vow and stayed silent
On that same day
This is what we learned (in the משנה)

steps.confusionAlert: The word בַּעַל here means the ארוס, the man she is engaged to. It does not mean a husband after full marriage.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
When did they say
"If the husband dies, the authority reverts to the father"

phrases.aramaic: בִּזְמַן שֶׁלֹּא שָׁמַע הַבַּעַל קוֹדֶם שֶׁיָּמוּת
phrases.english: When the husband did not hear the vow before he died
Or he heard and was silent

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שֶׁשָּׁמַע וְהֵפֵר וּמֵת בּוֹ בַּיּוֹם
phrases.english: Or he heard and cancelled, and died on that same day
This is what we learned:
phrases.notes: The ברייתא is pointing to a משנה later in this פרק (70a).

phrases.english: If the husband dies, the authority reverts to the father.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: אֵימָתַי אָמְרוּ מֵת הַבַּעַל נִתְרוֹקְנָה רְשׁוּת לָאָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a ברייתא brought to answer the question from Step 8 about whether the ארוס cuts or weakens the vow.
steps.raayaObject: The question of whether the ארוס's הפרה cuts away his share or weakens the whole vow.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא explaining when the father's power to cancel becomes complete after the ארוס dies, tied to the משנה 'מֵת הַבַּעַל נִתְרוֹקְנָה רְשׁוּת לָאָב'.
